items.item_text: Current license to practice clinical psychology in the State of California.
Experience supervising psychology trainees or clinicians working toward licensure.
Must be able to work various hours and locations based on business needs.
Employment is subject to a criminal background check and pre-employment physical.
Ph.D. or Psy.D. in Clinical Psychology or a closely related field that qualifies for California licensure.
Prior experience conducting diagnostic evaluations of children with autism or suspected ASD.
Experience conducting diagnostic evaluations of infants and toddlers ages 12–36 months.
Experience administering and interpreting standardized psychological, developmental, and/or diagnostic assessments.
Experience administering the ADOS or ADOS-2.
Experience in research setting and/or presenting to groups.
Experience with developmental assessments such as the Mullen Scales of Early Learning.
Experience working with both children with autism/developmental concerns and typically developing children.
Previous clinical research experience.

The UCSD Autism Center of Excellence is part of the Department of Neurosciences, an internationally recognized department within the UCSD School of Medicine, comprised of 152 Faculty, 25 Research and Project Scientists, 40 Postdocs, 25 Clinical Education, Administrative and Business Office staff with ~150 Research lab staff.

We are seeking an enthusiastic and collaborative licensed clinical psychologist to join our multidisciplinary research team focused on autism and early child development. Our program conducts NIH-, industry-, and philanthropically funded research aimed at advancing the early identification of autism, understanding its developmental and biological origins, and developing improved diagnostic and prognostic approaches. This position offers flexibility depending upon the candidate's interests. The psychologist may work full time in a clinical capacity or may choose a combined clinical-research position consisting of approximately four days per week of clinical work and one day per week devoted to research activities.

The primary responsibility of the position is conducting comprehensive diagnostic and developmental evaluations of children with autism, suspected autism, and other developmental concerns, as well as typically developing children participating in research studies. The psychologist typically conducts approximately 8 assessment sessions per week in a full-time clinical role. Responsibilities may include: conducting diagnostic evaluations for autism and other developmental conditions; administering, scoring, and interpreting standardized diagnostic, developmental, and psychometric assessments; writing a summary evaluation report; providing clinical impressions and communicating assessment results to families; collaborating with members of the multidisciplinary research team; and mentoring undergraduate students and/or supervising or providing clinical guidance to trainees and non-licensed psychologists working toward clinical licensure, as appropriate.

Additionally, the Psychologist may perform research activities. The duties may include: participating in the development and implementation of research protocols; developing or evaluating new approaches to the early identification and characterization of autism; developing novel behavioral and diagnostic assessment methods; conducting research experiments with infants, toddlers, and children; participating in data analysis and interpretation; contributing to scientific presentations, abstracts, and manuscripts; and collaborating with investigators and other members of the research team on ongoing and new research projects. Perform other duties as assigned.
Background in experimental design and statistics.
Knowledge of psychodiagnostic procedures and tests, such as the ADOS and Mullen Scales of Early Learning.
Bilingual English/Spanish skills preferred but are not required.
Ability to interview, perform psychological assessment, perform psychodiagnoses, plan and implement a variety of case dispositions.
Ability to develop scientific documents from collected data and present findings at scientific and educational venues.
Ability to interact easily and functionally with colleagues; ability to work well independently or as part of a team.
Demonstrated organizational skills.
Theoretical and experiential knowledge of autism.
Ability to relate warmly, humanely , sensitively, and empathically to others.
Demonstrated writing and editing skills and computer literacy with Windows, WordPerfect, Microsoft Word, and Excel
Knowledge of basic psychological science.
Ability to communicate clearly and effectively orally and in writing. Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
Ability to work with diverse populations and tradtionally underrepresented client groups.
Ability to work effectively and collaboratively as part of a multidisciplinary clinical research team.
Knowledge of the current laws, procedures and ethical principles that govern the practice of psychology, including services suggested or information disclosed by telephone.
